item.title: M5-brane source charges, Chern--Connes pairings and noncommutative compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.31674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate a source-adapted Chern--Connes description of M5-brane magnetic charge in physically motivated noncommutative and quotient linking sectors. The starting point is the local codimension-five geometry of an M5-brane source: the magnetic charge is measured on a four-dimensional link. In the smooth local model the link is the ordinary four-sphere, and the pairing reduces to the standard flux integral of the M-theory four-form field strength. The construction is motivated by the published even-codimensional Noncommutative Foliation Invariant (NCFI for short), where Connes' transverse fundamental cyclic cocycle is paired with an even transverse-geometric \(K\)-class. For an M5-brane the relevant codimension is odd, so the required odd \(K\)-class is supplied instead by the boundary map of the source/linking extension. Noncommutative or groupoid algebras are used only when they arise from physical mechanisms: Matrix/M-theory compactification on noncommutative tori, reduction to D-branes in background \(B\)-fields, large \(C\)-field M5 limits, or quotient/orbifold source links. The result is a topological charge formula, not a derivation of the full M5-brane dynamics or of the complete M-theory action.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis P. Zois

item.title: Higher \v{C}ech derived functors via Galois theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.32507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We explore sufficient conditions for the higher \v{C}ech derived functors of a Birkhoff reflector to agree with its ordinary, Barr-Beck comonadic homology. Using categorical Galois theory together with a spectral-sequence argument, we prove that this is the case for the reflector from any semi-abelian variety onto a subvariety: for every $n\geq 1$, the $n$th \v{C}ech derived functor of the reflector coincides with its $(n+1)$st comonadic homology object. More generally, the comparison holds for any Birkhoff reflector of a semi-abelian category equipped with a comonad satisfying Quillen's conditions.
item.dc:creator: Florent Afsa, Tim Van der Linden

item.title: $G_0$ of complete split toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.32831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves for complete split toric surfaces having a smooth 2-dimensional cone in its fan. We show that it is free abelian, of rank equal to the number of rays in the fan. We give a partial generalization of this to all complete split toric varieties.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Shen

item.title: Atiyah duality for motivic spectra
item.description: arXiv:2403.01561v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that Atiyah duality holds in the $\infty$-category of non-$\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectra over arbitrary derived schemes: every smooth projective scheme is dualizable with dual given by the Thom spectrum of its negative tangent bundle. The Gysin maps recently constructed by L. Tang are a key ingredient in the proof. We then present several applications. First, we study $\mathbb A^1$-colocalization, which transforms any module over the $\mathbb A^1$-invariant sphere into an $\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectrum without changing its values on smooth projective schemes. This can be applied to all known $p$-adic cohomology theories and gives a new elementary approach to "logarithmic" or "tame" cohomology theories; it recovers for instance the logarithmic crystalline cohomology of strict normal crossings compactifications over perfect fields and shows that the latter is independent of the choice of compactification. Second, we prove a motivic Landweber exact functor theorem, associating a motivic spectrum to any graded formal group law classified by a flat map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Using this theorem, we compute the ring of $\mathbb P^1$-stable cohomology operations on the algebraic K-theory of qcqs derived schemes, and we prove that rational motivic cohomology is an idempotent motivic spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Toni Annala, Marc Hoyois, Ryomei Iwasa

item.title: Eventually periodic resolutions with applications to integral group rings
item.description: arXiv:2510.18748v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a general construction of eventually periodic projective resolutions for modules over the quotient of a ring by a regular central element. Our approach combines the iterated mapping cone technique with the higher homotopies of Shamash. The periodic part of each resolution comes from a matrix factorization of the central element. The construction is applied to the integral group rings of quotients of groups of finite cohomological dimension by infinite cyclic central subgroups. We give explicit calculations for several families of groups, including hyperbolic triangle groups and the mapping class group of the plane with four punctures.
item.dc:creator: Sean P. Carroll

item.title: Quantum real projective spaces as quantum CW-complexes via topological graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.02017v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use the notion and properties of topological graphs to construct a quantum CW complex for quantum real projective spaces. This construction mirrors the CW complex construction in the classical case. Moreover, we introduce multipullback even-spheres as boundaries of noncommutative "cylinders" and show that they admit a gluing akin to the gluing of balls to the ends of a hollow closed cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Atul Gothe
